results.question: Why was Apple's tax rate in 2024 so much higher than the standard US federal rate?
results.answer: Apple's effective tax rate for 2024 was higher than the statutory federal income tax rate primarily due to a one-time income tax charge of $10.2 billion, net, related to the State Aid Decision [E1][E4]. Additionally, state income taxes contributed to the higher rate [E1]. These factors were partially offset by a lower effective tax rate on foreign earnings, the impact of the U.S. federal R&D credit, and tax benefits from share-based compensation [E1]. The specific components showing the difference between the provision for income taxes and the computed expected tax (based on the 21% statutory rate) include state taxes, net of federal effect ($1,162 million), the impact of the State Aid Decision ($10,246 million), earnings of foreign subsidiaries (-$5,311 million), research and development credit, net (-$1,397 million), excess tax benefits from equity awards (-$893 million), and other items ($10 million) [E4].

results.question: What are the six core functions in version 2.0 of the NIST Cybersecurity Framework?
results.answer: The six core functions in version 2.0 of the NIST Cybersecurity Framework are GOVERN, IDENTIFY, PROTECT, DETECT, RESPOND, and RECOVER [E1][E3].

judge_claims.claim: The six core functions in version 2.0 of the NIST Cybersecurity Framework are GOVERN, IDENTIFY, PROTECT, DETECT, RESPOND, and RECOVER
judge_claims.evidence_quote:
• PROTECT (PR) — Safeguards to manage the organization’s cybersecurity risks are used.
... 
• DETECT (DE) — Possible cybersecurity attacks and compromises are found and analyzed.
... 
• RESPOND (RS) — Actions regarding a detected cybersecurity incident are taken.
... 
• RECOVER (RC) — Assets and operations affected by a cybersecurity incident are restored.

results.question: Why is GOVERN drawn at the middle of the framework's wheel diagram?
results.answer: GOVERN is drawn in the center of the wheel because it informs how an organization will implement the other five Functions [E1]. Additionally, GOVERN provides outcomes to inform what an organization may do to achieve and prioritize the outcomes of the other five Functions in the context of its mission and stakeholder expectations [E2].

results.question: What are the names of the four tiers used to describe how rigorous an organization's cybersecurity risk management is?
results.answer: The four tiers used to describe an organization's cybersecurity risk governance and management practices are Partial (Tier 1), Risk Informed (Tier 2), Repeatable (Tier 3), and Adaptive (Tier 4) [E4]. These tiers reflect a progression from informal, ad hoc responses to approaches that are agile, risk-informed, and continuously improving [E1].

judge_claims.claim: The four tiers used to describe an organization's cybersecurity risk governance and management practices are Partial (Tier 1), Risk Informed (Tier 2), Repeatable (Tier 3), and Adaptive (Tier 4)
judge_claims.evidence_quote: There are four Tiers: Partial (Tier 1), Risk Informed (Tier 2), Repeatable (Tier 3), and Adaptive (Tier 4).

judge_claims.claim: These tiers reflect a progression from informal, ad hoc responses to approaches that are agile, risk-informed, and continuously improving
judge_claims.evidence_quote: The Tiers, as shown in Fig. 4 and notionally illustrated in Appendix B, reflect an organization’s practices for managing cybersecurity risk as Partial (Tier 1), Risk Informed (Tier 2), Repeatable (Tier 3), and Adaptive (Tier 4). The Tiers describe a progression from informal, ad hoc responses to approaches that are agile, risk-informed, and continuously improving.

results.question: Which functions help stop incidents before they happen, and which help deal with them afterwards?
results.answer: The Functions that help prevent and prepare for incidents are GOVERN, IDENTIFY, and PROTECT [E2]. The Functions that help discover and manage incidents (dealing with them afterwards) are GOVERN, DETECT, RESPOND, and RECOVER [E2]. Specifically, the DETECT Function enables the timely discovery of attacks and compromises [E1], while the RESPOND Function supports actions to contain the effects of cybersecurity incidents [E1]. The RECOVER Function supports the restoration of normal operations after an incident [E1].

results.question: Why did the authors end up preferring the collapsed tree approach over tree traversal?
results.answer: The authors preferred the collapsed tree approach because it offers greater flexibility than tree traversal [E1]. Specifically, by searching through all nodes simultaneously, the collapsed tree retrieves information at the correct level of granularity for a given question [E1]. In contrast, tree traversal maintains a constant ratio of nodes from each level regardless of the question, meaning the ratio of higher-order thematic information to granular details remains the same [E1]. Additionally, empirical testing on 20 stories from the QASPER dataset showed that the collapsed tree approach consistently performs better [E1].

judge_claims.claim: The authors preferred the collapsed tree approach because it offers greater flexibility than tree traversal.
judge_claims.evidence_quote: The collapsed tree approach consistently performs better. We believe collapsed tree retrieval is better due to offering greater flexibility than tree traversal; i.e., by searching through all the nodes simultaneously, it retrieves information that is at the correct level of granularity for a given question.

judge_claims.claim: By searching through all nodes simultaneously, the collapsed tree retrieves information at the correct level of granularity for a given question.
judge_claims.evidence_quote: We believe collapsed tree retrieval is better due to offering greater flexibility than tree traversal; i.e., by searching through all the nodes simultaneously, it retrieves information that is at the correct level of granularity for a given question.

judge_claims.claim: In contrast, tree traversal maintains a constant ratio of nodes from each level regardless of the question, meaning the ratio of higher-order thematic information to granular details remains the same.
judge_claims.evidence_quote: In comparison, while using tree traversal with the same values of d and k, the ratio of nodes from each level of the tree will be constant. So, the ratio of higher-order thematic information to granular details will remain the same regardless of the question.

judge_claims.claim: Additionally, empirical testing on 20 stories from the QASPER dataset showed that the collapsed tree approach consistently performs better.
judge_claims.evidence_quote: We tested both approaches on 20 stories from the QASPER dataset. Figure 3 shows the performance of tree traversal with different top- sizes and collapsed tree with different maximum token numbers. The collapsed tree approach consistently performs better.

results.question: What is the trade-off between using big chunks and small chunks?
results.answer: The trade-off between using big chunks and small chunks involves balancing context, retrieval recall, process time, and faithfulness. Larger chunks provide more context, which enhances comprehension but increases process time [E1]. Conversely, smaller chunks improve retrieval recall and reduce processing time but may lack sufficient context [E1]. Finding the optimal chunk size requires a balance between metrics such as faithfulness (whether the response matches retrieved texts) and relevancy (whether retrieved texts match queries) [E1].
